line: Alan Fong. Fong's Pharmacy, on Grand. I drop off the seniors' pill organizers here on Thursdays. Fourteen boxes, all labelled. You're new?
Alan Fong, Fong's Pharmacy. Dropping off insulin pens for Dr. Haddad's people. You look like you've been waiting a while.
choice1: Long enough. Nice to meet you.
choice3: I'd rather not chat right now.

line: I came from Hong Kong at twelve. My kids, Ethan and Chloe, don't speak Cantonese. Chloe can order dim sum. That's the whole inheritance.
Honestly? No. My kids won't need any of this, and that's fine. Ethan's applying to engineering schools. Nobody there asks if he knows his tones.
Then he'll take a class, like anybody. My mother spent her life with one foot in Kowloon. I spent mine getting both feet here. I'm not sorry.
Mrs. Chen asked me to print her labels in Chinese. I said she should learn 'twice a day with food.' She called me a bad boy. I'm fifty-seven.
choice2: Both on the label would help.

line: Mr. Guo wants me on the board again. Every year he asks, every year I say the same thing: I'll fill the pill boxes, I won't sit through the meetings.
Advice I gave my nephew: put your English name on the business card. Not instead. First. People call back the name they can say.
Ethan's soccer team has a barbecue at our place Sunday. Twenty families, one grill, my wife in charge. Come. Nobody talks about the old country.
Three customers asked me this week if the pharmacy reports to immigration. It doesn't. I've been a citizen thirty years and I checked my passport drawer last night.
choice2: You've got nothing to worry about.

line: The state is paying for translated prescription labels now. Good for the seniors. My worry is the young ones stop bothering with English.
choice1: The labels are for the seniors.
choice2: They'll learn it at work, like you did.

line: You're at the center every time I come. Careful. Guo will have you running the festival, and then it's your whole life.
I hear you're at the library, the merchants' thing, everywhere. Good. That's how it works. Ten years, nobody asks where you're from.
Alan is counting boxes and doesn't look up.
Fourteen boxes, thirteen labels. Somebody's Tuesday pills are missing. Not now.
